faqLeft.q: What engine does the Mercedes S500 use?
faqLeft.a: It depends on the year. From 2008 to 2017 (W221 and W222 generations), the S500 used the M278 4.7-litre V8 petrol engine. From 2020 onwards (W223), it switched to the M256 3.0-litre inline-six petrol with mild-hybrid assistance — a completely different engine. Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your car has.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes S500 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: It depends on the engine. Rebuilds start from £3,200 for the M256 and £4,500 for the M278. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my S500?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the M278 or the M256 before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M278 S500 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace timing chains, valve seals and coolant system components as standard on every M278 rebuild.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild M256 S500 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The M256 is a generally reliable modern engine, and we service it to the same high standard as our other S500 rebuilds, replacing timing chains, bearings and water pump as required.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used S500 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my S500 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an S500 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most S500 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
